name: french lentils
instructions:
THE FRENCH LENTILS MEGA RECIPE — three variants, merged 2026-11-13 from creamy french lentils + sherry french lentils:
- VARIANT A — CREAMY FRENCH LENTILS: the gravy-core stew (mustard + cream + potato).
- VARIANT B — AMY'S LENTIL SOUP: the clone, work in progress.
- VARIANT C — SHERRY/BUTTER CLASSIC LE PUY: the instapot side.

BUILD-DEPENDENT RULINGS: DIJON is structural (silent) in A but CLASHING in C; TARRAGON is C's finish herb but CLASHING in A (fine-herbs rule). Both live in secondary.

=== VARIANT A — CREAMY FRENCH LENTILS (THE GRAVY-CORE STEW) ===

CREAMY FRENCH LENTILS — a french lentil stew built on a PUREED-MUSHROOM GRAVY CORE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour). The gravy core is a vegetarian way of making something 'meaty', but it's NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN — MUSTARD + CREAM + POTATO do the flavor injection. See [[pub-style-lentils]] for the dark-ale/pickle cousin built on the same core.

=== THE GRAVY CORE ===

- pureed portabella mushrooms (food processor or blender)
- whole lentils
- tomato paste (small, cooked hard — necessary but should NOT be tasted)
- dark bouillon / stock
- butter
- flour (light roux)

=== THE FRENCH INJECTION ===

- dijon mustard + heavy cream (stirred in near the end — SILENT; the lentil/potato starch absorbs them)
- potatoes (finely chopped — the sweetness and savoriness the base lacks)

=== VEGETABLES ===

- The traditional ONION / CELERY / CARROT soffrito.
- LEEKS are welcome too — they bridge both registers.

=== HERBS ===

- FRESH THYME preferred. Nothing else — fine herbs are clashing, and ROSEMARY is clashing too (this build is a celery + tomato forward stew — see the rosemary rule in [[shittake-lentil-soup]]; an older 'rosemary also allowed' line stood here and was stale against the clashing list).

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. SOFFRITO IN BUTTER + OLIVE OIL: sauté finely chopped yellow onion, celery, and carrots (and leek if using) until softened.
2. PUREED MUSHROOMS: puree the portabellas, add to the pot, and cook down until reduced and deepened in color.
3. TOMATO PASTE — SMALL, COOKED HARD: a small spoonful, cooked into the fat until it darkens a shade. It should not be tasteable in the finished stew.
4. FLOUR — LIGHT ROUX: dust flour over the base and stir to coat.
5. HERBS: fresh thyme (or a light hand of rosemary). Salt and black pepper.
6. POTATOES + LENTILS: fold in finely diced potatoes and lentils together (same cook rate).
7. DARK BOUILLON / STOCK: pour in generously — the primary liquid.
8. SLOW COOK covered until lentils and potatoes are tender.
9. MUSTARD + CREAM — NEAR THE END: a spoonful of dijon and a splash of cream, stirred in. Both silent in the finished stew.
10. OPTIONAL STARCH SLURRY at the end if the broth reads thin (usually not needed — the roux + potatoes carry it).

=== VARIANT B — AMY'S LENTIL SOUP (WORK IN PROGRESS) ===

A clone of the Amy's-brand lentil soup. CURIOUSLY, the Amy's label declares NO MUSHROOMS, NO STOCK, NO BUTTER, NO VINEGAR — but does say there are SPICES.

What I tried, and it seemed to get close:
1. PURÉE + PRESSURE-COOK AN ONION SLURRY first, before cooking with the celery / carrot / potatoes / lentils.
2. SPICES: cumin, coriander, and fennel, plus A LITTLE PORCINI POWDER.

This variant is a WORK IN PROGRESS.

=== VARIANT C — SHERRY/BUTTER CLASSIC LE PUY (INSTAPOT SIDE) ===

The classic french le puy lentil side — REDEEMED (was briefly retired; see notes). The whole point: a SIDE you can throw into an instapot WITHOUT a multi-stage stew flavor-building process. No sauté, minimal liquid, and the secret finish is SHERRY VINEGAR + BUTTER.

SERVES 4 as a side.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 cup dried LE PUY LENTILS, rinsed (the small dark-green french lentils — they hold their shape; don't sub red or brown)
- 1 small yellow onion, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 1 carrot, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 1 celery stalk, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 2-3 garlic cloves, chopped — NOT sautéed
- 1 BAY LEAF (important)
- chicken stock + water — JUST ENOUGH TO COVER the lentils (see the liquid rule)
- salt (go light if the stock is salted) and black pepper

FINISH:
- SHERRY VINEGAR (must be sherry — see notes)
- BUTTER (necessary)
- DRIED TARRAGON (the best herbal finish here)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. EVERYTHING IN THE POT RAW: lentils, chopped onion/garlic/celery/carrot, bay leaf. No sauté step — especially in an instapot, just chopped up and thrown in is fine.
2. LIQUID: chicken stock + water to JUST COVER the lentils — no more. It cooks down to a lentil SIDE, not a stew.
3. PRESSURE COOK: high, 13 minutes (current practice; maybe 15 — see the timing note).
4. FINISH: fish out the bay leaf. SHERRY VINEGAR + BUTTER stirred through hot, dried tarragon, salt and pepper to taste.
notes:
=== MERGED 2026-11-13 — THE THREE-VARIANT MEGA RECIPE ===

Creamy french lentils (variant A, with its Amy's work-in-progress as variant B) and sherry french lentils (variant C) merged into one french-lentils house. A is a stew, B is a soup clone, C is deliberately a SIDE and not a stew.

=== BUILD-DEPENDENT INGREDIENTS (SECONDARY) ===

- DIJON MUSTARD: variant A structural — stirred in near the end, SILENT depth. Variant C CLASHING — the first-cook dijon + red-wine finish was overturned by sherry vinegar + butter.
- TARRAGON: variant C's finish herb (dried tarragon, the best herbal finish there). Variant A CLASHING — fine herbs are clashing in the gravy-core stew.
- The LENTIL ITSELF splits: variant A takes standard whole lentils; variant C is LE PUY specifically (identity of the dish — they hold their shape).

=== VARIANT A — NOTES (THE CREAMY STEW) ===

=== RENAMED FROM 'MUSHROOMED LENTILS FRENCH' (2026-10-31) ===

The mushroomed-lentils taxonomy is dissolved — these were really different stews. The PUREED-MUSHROOM GRAVY CORE (pureed mushrooms + whole lentils + tomato paste + dark bouillon + butter + flour) is still the mechanism that separates this from the cookbook's other lentil dishes (e.g. variant C of this same recipe, which has no gravy core at all) — but the dish's identity is the CREAMY FRENCH character, so that leads the name now.

THE GRAVY CORE IS NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN — proven by experiment (stock + vegetables + gravy base alone makes a dull stew). The injection kit here: MUSTARD + CREAM + POTATO. ([[pub-style-lentils]]'s ale + pickle build injects dark ale + pickle juice + cumin/caraway into the same core.)

=== THE FRENCH INJECTION — MUSTARD + CREAM + POTATO ===

- POTATOES: add a sweetness and savoriness the base doesn't have. Finely diced (small dice) so they cook with the lentils and dissolve starch into the broth. Not filler — the missing flavor dimension.
- MUSTARD + CREAM: do a ton of heavy lifting, SILENTLY — done carefully you don't taste either, because the starch load from lentils + potatoes absorbs them (same silent-ingredient logic as [[spinach-ricotta]]'s miso/nooch rule). They round and enrich without announcing themselves.

=== TOMATO — NECESSARY BUT SHOULDN'T BE TASTED ===

Tomato paste is part of the shared core: its darkened concentration does real depth-and-color work. But it should NOT read as tomato in the finished stew. Two mechanisms keep it in line:
- SMALL QUANTITY, cooked hard into the fat.
- THE PUREED MUSHROOMS TAME IT: the mushroom base grounds and darkens so tomato contributes depth without running the show. (Same mechanism in the anglo-germanic sibling, where dark ale helps too.)
Counterintuitively, this french version needs LESS tomato paste than the anglo one, even though the anglo one looks darker — french ingredients mesh with tomato; the anglo version's bitter base fights it and needs more. Calibrate by register, not color.

=== VEGETABLES — ONION / CELERY / CARROT (LEEKS BRIDGE) ===

The french version takes the traditional soffrito: onion + celery + carrot. Leeks are welcome in both versions of this pair — they bridge the two registers.

=== WINE — A RATATOUILLE SITUATION: WORKS BUT UNNECESSARY ===

White wine went through the full arc here (primary → clashing → re-diagnosed as balance-dependent). Final stance: it's a RATATOUILLE SITUATION — wine works, but the dish doesn't need it, and the version without is just as good. Save the wine for dishes where it does structural work. (If you do add it: modest amount, and make sure the butter/flour/potato balance is present to absorb it.)

=== HERBS — FRESH THYME PREFERRED; ROSEMARY ALLOWED; FINE HERBS CLASHING ===

The herb slot for both recipes in this pair is ROSEMARY/THYME ONLY. The french version PREFERS FRESH THYME; rosemary is allowed (light hand). FINE HERBS ARE CLASHING — parsley, basil, tarragon, dill all read wrong against the mushroomed gravy base. (The anglo-germanic sibling prefers rosemary instead.)

=== REFERENCE — VALIDATED EXPERIMENTS (READ-ONLY LOG) ===

The experiments that produced this recipe remain valid; kept condensed for reference:
- STOCK + VEGETABLES + GRAVY ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH — the injection kit is required (this is what forced the mustard/cream/potato discovery).
- BUTTER + FLOUR + MUSTARD was the original 'generic to home run' enrichment finding; cream joined later.
- MUSTARD-AND-MUSHROOM PAIRING: dijon + mushroom fills the same structural role miso + mushroom filled in the retired lentil wellington — fermented condiment + mushroom = enhanced meat-analog umami. When a mushroom-forward dish reads flat, reach for the register-appropriate fermented condiment.
- WINE RE-DIAGNOSIS: earlier wine failures were balance failures (too much wine or not enough starch/butter), not the wine itself.
- PUREED-NOT-CHOPPED: chopped mushrooms give a chunkier, less integrated dish; the puree is the base's mechanism.
- STOCK PREFERRED, BOUILLON OKAY: real stock has the gentler layered body; bouillon works with a lighter hand than the package says.
- The broader three-register theory lives in articles/stew-registers.md (read-only reference).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[pub-style-lentils]]: the anglo-dark pub stew, two builds in one recipe — its ale + pickle build runs the same gravy core with the anglo-germanic injection (dark ale + pickle juice + cumin/caraway); its marmite build is the Jamie cottage-pie line served on mash. The contrast pair.
- [[shittake-lentil-soup]]: the clean dark-stock soup — the lentil + mushroom DNA's other home.
- [[milk-stout-braised-beef]]: the meat expression of the anglo-germanic register.
- [[french-chicken-soup]]: the committed-french-broth cousin with chicken.
- minestrone-soup: the committed-italian-tomato path — what this recipe's demoted-tomato logic deliberately is not.

=== THE ROSEMARY RULE (UNSOLVED — FROM THE OLD STEW FAMILY) ===

ROSEMARY BELONGS WHERE A DARK ANCHOR LIVES — ale/marmite ([[pub-style-lentils]], both builds) or dark stock ([[shittake-lentil-soup]]) — where it gives LIFT. In the celery + tomato forward stews (this one; the retired italian mushroomed lentils) it tastes ORTHOGONAL — nothing pairs with it. Competing theories: the dark anchor; 'something meaty' for it to grip; or the CELERY itself vetoing it — but [[chicken-pot-pie]] has celery AND rosemary happily, so no theory is clean. UNSOLVED. This recipe likes THYME for its own reasons (mustard + cream).

=== VARIANT B — NOTES (AMY'S LENTIL SOUP, WORK IN PROGRESS) ===

The Amy's-brand lentil soup as a separate variant of this recipe. The label is the curiosity: Amy's declares NO mushrooms, stock, butter, or vinegar — but does say there are spices. So the meaty depth has to come from somewhere else.

THE ONION SLURRY LEAD: pureeing + pressure-cooking an onion slurry BEFORE cooking with the celery/carrot/potatoes/lentils seemed to get close — the onion purée may be doing the body/depth work that the main build gets from the pureed-mushroom gravy core.

THE SPICE GUESS: cumin, coriander, and fennel, with a little porcini powder (the porcini is my addition — Amy's declares no mushrooms).

Still a work in progress — log adjustments as they come.

=== VARIANT C — NOTES (SHERRY/BUTTER LE PUY SIDE) ===

=== REDEEMED (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

Retired after the first cook (soffrito + broth boring; cream/mustard/vinegar too much; submerged format read as a failed stew; 'no slot left to win') — then redeemed with the discoveries below. The retirement diagnosis was right ('this doesn't want to be a stew') and every fix follows from it: minimal liquid, no flavor-building stages, and a finish that seasons a SIDE rather than building a stew.

=== THE SECRET — SHERRY VINEGAR + BUTTER ===

The secret ingredient pair is SHERRY VINEGAR AND BUTTER — not red wine vinegar, and not mustard (the first cook's dijon + red-wine finish is overturned). It MUST be sherry — other vinegars are TOO HARSH. And the butter is NECESSARY. (Against the old canonical-finish question: the peasant-classical butter-plus-vinegar answer beat the bistro dijon-vinaigrette answer — with the vinegar upgraded to sherry.)

=== THE LIQUID RULE — JUST COVER, NO MORE ===

Fill the pot with just enough chicken stock + water to COVER the lentils, so it cooks down to a LENTIL SIDE and not a stew. The first cook's too-easy-to-become-soup problem was a liquid-quantity problem.

=== NO SAUTÉ — EVERYTHING RAW IN THE POT ===

The onion/garlic/celery/carrot do NOT get sautéed beforehand. Especially in an instapot: chopped up and thrown in with a bay leaf is fine. This is the point of the recipe — no multi-stage flavor building.

=== HERBS — DRIED TARRAGON IS THE FINISH; BAY LEAF IN THE COOK ===

DRIED TARRAGON is the best herbal finish here — better than thyme, certainly better than rosemary or parsley. I like tarragon in this dish MORE than I like it in chicken stews. BAY LEAF is important in the cook itself.

=== PRESSURE TIMING — 13 MIN, MAYBE 15; PRESOAK OPEN QUESTION ===

Current practice: 13 MINUTES at high pressure. Might bump to 15 — the risk at longer times is DESTROYING THE CARROTS, not the lentils (le puy holds; the vegetables are the fragile part). OPEN QUESTION: perhaps a PRESOAK + 10 minutes at high pressure is better — soaked lentils cook faster, which would spare the carrots. Untested.

=== FIRST COOK — HISTORICAL RESULTS (KEPT FOR THE RECORD) ===

- PRESSURE TIME: 8 min high wasn't enough; +3 was sort of enough (superseded by the 13-min current practice above).
- The dijon + red wine vinegar finish read great on a spoonful but didn't hold up — superseded by sherry + butter.
- Rosemary would be awful here — still clashing.

=== LE PUY SPECIFICALLY ===

Le puy lentils hold their shape through cooking — the identity of the dish. Standard brown lentils go soft and muddy; red lentils dissolve entirely (wrong dish).

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[lentil-cream-salad]]: the cold expression of french lentils (cream vinaigrette + endives). This is the warm side.
- Variant A of this same recipe: the rich gravy-core cousin — that's the stew; this build is deliberately not one.
- [[jaffrey-mint-lentils]]: the indian whole-lentil counterpart.
- [[basque-pepper-stews]]: the other place sherry vinegar is queued (the iberian swing).
why_i_like_this_recipe: It's a side that can be thrown into an instapot without a multi-stage stew flavor-building process.
